cards.text: Solomon, king of Israel and son of David, is about to build the house of the LORD. This is the BIG one, friend. The Bible dates this moment by counting all the way back to when Israel came out of Egypt.

cards.question: Solomon begins building the house of the LORD in the ___ year after the Israelites came out of Egypt.
Solomon starts building the house of the LORD in his very first year as king.

cards.text: Up it goes: a house sixty cubits long, twenty wide and thirty high, with a porch out front, narrow windows up high, and three floors of side rooms around it, all roofed with cedar. The stones were cut at the quarry, so no hammer, no chisel, no iron tool was heard at the temple while it was being built. A construction site with NO noise? Friend, I've heard one man hang ONE shelf and it sounded like a drum solo.
Then the word of the LORD comes to Solomon about this temple he's building. Friend, when GOD shows up on your job site, you stop what you're doing and you LISTEN.

cards.question: God says He'll fulfill through Solomon the promise He made to David, but there's an 'if.' What does Solomon need to do?

answers.text: Walk in God's statutes and keep His commandments
Bring a thousand offerings to the new altar
Build the temple bigger than any palace

cards.question: God's promise to David will come through Solomon no matter how Solomon lives.
Then God says what He'll do for His people: He will ___ among the Israelites and will not abandon His people Israel.

cards.text: So Solomon builds the temple and finishes it, then works through the details inside and out, all the way to the inner courtyard. The standout is the Most Holy Place, made for the ark of the covenant of the LORD, with two olive wood cherubim whose wingtips touch in the middle, and GOLD over the whole interior. I spent years under a takeout menu, and this man's got GOLD on the inside.

The foundation went down in the fourth year of Solomon's reign. In the eleventh year, in the month of Bul, the temple is finished in every detail and according to every specification. EVERY detail, friend. I can't finish one batch without forgetting the timer.

cards.question: From the foundation in Solomon's fourth year to the finish in his eleventh, how long did building the temple take?

cards.text: We'll pause right here, friend. Don't you DARE take that apron off. This story keeps going.

findings.problem: The card cites only 1 Kings 6:1, but that verse does not say Solomon was David's son. That relationship appears later in 1 Kings 6:12, so the citation does not cover everything the card tells.

rule.text: Every story card cites the verses it tells, from the first verse it uses to the last, no wider and no narrower.

findings.problem: The blank asks the baker to supply the unseen wording of 1 Kings 6:13. The earlier cards discuss the temple and Solomon's obedience but do not develop the idea of God dwelling with His people, so this is principally a wording guess rather than a meaning the baker has been equipped to reason out.

rule.text: The rule against guessing the next words of a line (see below) applies to every passage, and to fill in the blank too. The blank tests meaning the baker can reason out, not wording they haven't seen.

findings.problem: Several non-opening story cards exceed the sentence limit: card 4 has four sentences, card 9 has three, card 10 has four, and card 12 has three.

rule.text: Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.
